intro: Chandrayaan-3 landed near the lunar south pole on August 23, 2023 — India's first soft landing on the Moon and the closest landing to the south pole by any nation. The Vikram lander deployed the Pragyan rover, which drove ~100 m across 14 days searching for water ice in permanently shadowed terrain. India became the fourth nation to soft-land on the Moon, after USSR, USA, and China.

images.caption: Chandrayaan-3 spacecraft stack during pre-launch integration at ISRO Sriharikota.
Pragyan rover — 26 kg, solar-powered, 6-wheeled. Designed to drive across the lunar south-pole regolith looking for volatiles.

images.caption: LVM3 ("Bahubali") launches Chandrayaan-3 — 40-day transit including multi-loop lunar capture, intentional slow trajectory to maximize fuel margin.

chapters.subtitle: Shiv Shakti Point, near lunar south pole — landed August 23, 2023

images.caption: Vikram lander on the south-polar surface — touchdown 69.37°S, the highest-latitude lunar landing ever performed.
Pragyan rover descending the ramp — first wheels at the lunar south pole, photographed by Vikram's onboard cameras.
